I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 45 years. I know every mu of it. My family has four mouths to feed, and the wheat-maize rotation is what keeps us with grain to eat. I also keep a patch of cotton for cash. I have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, but diesel for the pump costs money, and I am getting older, so I do not waste labor.

This year I will plant **5 mu to wheat-maize double cropping** and **2.7 mu to cotton**. It is early spring now, and my winter wheat is already in the ground. I sowed it last October with *Luyuan 502*, an improved variety that has done well here for years—reliable, not too fancy. I will top-dress it with about 55 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some compound fertilizer that gives about 20 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium. I will irrigate three times from the well: green-up, jointing, and heading. The wheat will need three pesticide sprays—insecticide twice and one fungicide spray when the weather turns damp. I rotary-tilled before sowing in autumn, so no more tillage now. If the weather cooperates, I expect 500 kg per mu.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I will put in summer maize immediately. Everyone here uses *Denghai 605*, a hybrid. I will seed it directly into the wheat stubble with no tillage—saves time and fuel. I will put down around 22 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu, irrigate twice (the big-trumpet stage and grain-filling), and spray three times for insects and weeds. I count on 550 kg per mu.

My 2.7 mu of cotton I will rotary-plough in spring and sow with *Guoxinmian*, an improved variety I trust. Cotton needs more fertilizer balance, so I will apply about 18 kg nitrogen, 15 kg phosphorus, and 15 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice and spray about 10 times through the season—cotton bollworm does not forgive laziness. I expect 275 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I do what the neighbors do, what my well allows, and what 45 years has taught me works.
